artigo.texto: 'Let Data Reign': Trump goes all in on controversial data centers Trump argued that data centers will make communities "successful and rich." President Donald Trump on Monday stressed his strong support for controversial data centers, a key issue ahead of midterm elections, with the president urging communities to "let Data Reign." "The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor. If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign," Trump wrote in a social media post on Monday morning. The president has long emphasized the importance of artificial intelligence advancement, repeatedly expressing his desire for the U.S. to beat China in the global AI race. "If we kill the Golden Goose, you will only have yourselves to blame. China could not be happier with this anti Data Center movement. Actually, they can’t believe it is happening!" Trump wrote. Data centers provide the computing power necessary to process large amounts of data, such as the kind needed to run AI systems. They typically house thousands of computer servers and require tremendous amounts of land, water for cooling, and energy, potentially straining local power grids, while employing few workers long-term, relative to their size. The issue of data centers has been a hot topic ahead of the midterm elections, with AI companies spending millions on congressional races and primaries for and against candidates on the issue of artificial intelligence regulation. Asked on Monday about Trump's post and how it might land ahead of the midterms, Vice President JD Vance said the president's message was focused on the economics around data centers. "What the president said about data centers is they're an important part of the AI economy. But when people build them, they have to build the power plants along with the data centers,” Vance said. Vance acknowledged the backlash surrounding data centers, expressing his belief that the concern stems from higher utility and electricity bills. But he argued that this wouldn't be a problem if companies take advantage of deregulation efforts. "I think probably 99% of the backlash to data centers has come in areas where building a data center means higher utility and higher electricity for the people on the ground," Vance said. "So I think what these companies have to do is take advantage of some of the federal deregulatory efforts that we've undertaken. If you build a data center, you should be putting power back into the grid, not taking it out. And if that is happening, I don't think the data centers are that controversial," Vance said. Earlier this month, the National Republican Senatorial Committee, the Senate GOP's campaign committee, wrote a memo to AI companies operating in Ohio and warned that backlash to data centers could hurt incumbent Republican Sen. John Husted’s chances at reelection. Texas Republican Gov. Greg Abbott also recently paused new data center projects to ensure compliance -- something that Trump had criticized as a "mistake." "I saw Texas the other day sort of is against data centers. I think it's a mistake. And I’m not taking positions, I just think it’s a mistake, because there are other communities that want it. When a community wants it, it means a lot of money is going to come into that community," Trump had said during a Punchbowl interview earlier this month. In the Punchbowl interview, the president expressed his belief that data centers are "tremendously important for the economics" and said they could be "bigger than oil."

CATL's Debrecen Lines Begin Trial Runs as Battery Maker Refreshes Storage Pricing and Adds European Freight Allies
Published on 09/25/2026 at 14:52 | Editorial boerse-global.de
CATL has moved its Hungarian manufacturing bet from blueprint to hardware. Trial operations began Tuesday on the first two cell production lines at the company's Debrecen plant, following the completion of all regulatory approvals. The runs are meant to calibrate equipment ahead of full-scale output, and once the site is finished it will carry a designed annual capacity of 100 gigawatt-hours, making it the group's largest production base outside China.
The milestone lands in a week when the world's biggest battery maker was busy on several other fronts at once — raising fresh capital at home, resetting prices on its energy-storage catalog, and widening a web of partnerships across Europe, China and North Africa.
A seventh green bond, and a storage lineup in motion
On the financing side, CATL closed its seventh green technology innovation bond of the year on Tuesday, pulling in 4.5 billion RMB. The issue splits into a 4.0 billion RMB tranche carrying a 1.49% coupon and a 500 million RMB tranche priced at 1.55%.
Alongside the fundraising, the company adjusted its storage product lineup. Listed entry prices for 280-ampere-hour storage cells were lifted to 0.470 RMB per watt-hour, while 314-ampere-hour cells now start at 0.403 RMB per watt-hour. For the first time, a 587-ampere-hour storage cell also appeared on the public list, with an entry price of 0.415 RMB per watt-hour. CATL characterized the moves to media as a routine adjustment.
Heavy trucks, DHL, Kuehne+Nagel — and a plant in Egypt
The commercial-vehicle push is advancing in parallel. At the launch of its new TECTRANS II platform, which is designed for a maximum range of up to 1,000 kilometers, CATL signed a memorandum of understanding with DHL Group aimed at decarbonizing European road-freight corridors. Days later came a second cooperation agreement, this one with Kuehne+Nagel, covering electrification concepts for European transport fleets as well as a pilot for Qiji battery-swap systems on heavy trucks in China.
Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL?
CATL is also exporting its model further afield. In Egypt, it struck a partnership with BME to assemble battery packs for heavy commercial vehicles, contributing technology licenses, production equipment and training. That plant opens with an initial annual capacity of 1 gigawatt-hour, with plans to scale to as much as 5 gigawatt-hours over the longer term.
Buyback underway, tax change absorbed
Management has been equally active on the capital-return front. On September 11, CATL bought back 604,293 of its own A-shares on the Shenzhen exchange, spending exactly 199,978,827.46 yuan on the transaction.

ST. THOMAS, ONT. – PowerCo Canada has named EllisDon Corporation the general contractor for its $7 billion St. Thomas gigafactory, marking a key milestone as the project advances into its next phase of construction.
The project is now moving into the core infrastructure and structural phases that will support future production.
Work includes the production-building shell, mechanical, electrical and plumbing installations, energy and utility systems and supporting site services. Approximately 60 EllisDon workers are currently onsite, expected to ramp up to roughly 1,300 workers at peak, alongside additional personnel supporting parallel project activities, a release reads.
At 1.5-million-square-feet, the plant will be the size of 210 football fields just for the factory alone. The entire industrial park itself amounts to 1,500 acres, or an area of 850 football fields.
“The PowerCo facility represents a transformative investment in Canada’s industrial future, and EllisDon is proud to play a role in its delivery,” said Max Mantha, president, construction at EllisDon in a statement. “As a Canadian-headquartered, employee-owned company, we are committed to building the infrastructure that will help support Canada’s growing electric vehicle and battery manufacturing sector. This project will create opportunities for skilled tradespeople, local businesses, and communities across southwestern Ontario, and we look forward to working with PowerCo and our partners on this landmark development.”
Ground was broken in 2025 on the project, with Magil Construction Canada leading foundation construction for three major buildings and Steelcon Group of Companies fabricating and erecting structural steel components.
PowerCo has stated it is also aligning the project’s timeline and product strategy “with evolving market demand, technological advancements and the Volkswagen Group’s long-term strategy.”
St. Thomas is now expected to begin operations in 2029. PowerCo had previously said initial battery production was targeted for 2027.
“The St. Thomas gigafactory remains a cornerstone of our North American strategy,” said Joel Karlsberg, chief procurement officer with PowerCo Canada.
“We are continuing to build now while determining how and when the facility scales over time. This is about getting the pacing right — not stepping back — to protect our long-term investment, support regional jobs, and position Canada, Ontario and St. Thomas to benefit in a dynamic and evolving market.”

Quem é Nestory Irankunda, ex-Bayern autor de golaço contra o Brasil
Jovem de 20 anos, com passagens por Bayern, Watford e Grasshoppers, abriu o placar para a Austrália contra a Seleção de Ancelotti
Nestory Irankunda, ponta de 20 anos do Sporting, de Portugal, e com passagem pelo Bayern de Munique, foi o responsável por abrir o placar para a Austrália contra a Seleção Brasileira.
O gol ocorreu no amistoso desta sexta-feira (25), na cidade de Townsville, em solo australiano, marcando o primeiro jogo do ciclo para a Copa do Mundo de 2030.
O jovem balançou as redes em uma bela cobrança de falta, superando o goleiro Hugo Souza, do Corinthians. Com isso, o time comandado por Carlo Ancelotti viu a Austrália sair na frente no confronto. Nos acréscimos, Rayan marcou de cabeça e empatou a partida.
Apesar da pouca idade, Irankunda já acumula uma história de superação. Seus pais são originários do Burundi, tendo fugido do país devido à guerra civil. Nestory nasceu em Kigoma, na Tanzânia, e foi levado para a Austrália quando tinha apenas três meses de vida.

— CommBank Socceroos (@Socceroos) September 25, 2026
A trajetória de Irankunda no futebol
Na Austrália, Irankunda cresceu longe do conflito e começou a se dedicar ao futebol desde cedo. Talentoso, ele fez sua estreia profissional pelo Adelaide United na temporada 2021/22, um dos clubes mais importantes do futebol local.
Seu desempenho de destaque no futebol australiano atraiu a atenção do gigante Bayern de Munique, da Alemanha, que o contratou em 2024. No entanto, o jogador não chegou a atuar pela equipe principal do clube bávaro.
O Bayern optou por emprestá-lo ao Grasshoppers, da Suíça, e posteriormente ao Watford, na Inglaterra. Atualmente, nesta temporada, Nestory Irankunda defende as cores do Sporting, em Portugal.
Considerado um dos grandes nomes da nova geração australiana, Irankunda participou da última Copa do Mundo, em que a Austrália chegou até a segunda fase, sendo eliminada pelo Egito.

Rayan salva no fim, e Brasil só empata com Austrália em amistoso pós-Copa
Com gol no último lance, time de Ancelotti voltou a apresentar dificuldades no 4-2-4
O Brasil voltou a jogar mal e só empatou com a Austrália no primeiro amistoso pós-Copa do Mundo na manhã desta sexta-feira (25). Em partida disputada no Estádio Queensland Country Bank, em Townsville, as equipes empataram em 1 a 1, graças a um gol de Rayan no último lance.
O time de Carlo Ancelotti encontrou problemas na primeira etapa, principalmente nos 20 minutos iniciais, quando a Austrália permaneceu no campo de ataque e levou sustos ao gol brasileiro. Estêvão chegou a abrir o placar no fim do primeiro tempo, mas o lance foi anulado por falta de Bruno Guimarães.
A Seleção foi mais ofensiva na segunda etapa, e criou as principais chances de gol com Raphinha e Estêvão. Apesar disso, quem fez o primeiro gol foi Irankunda, com um belo gol de falta para a seleção australiana. O lance gerou discussão sobre o posicionamento de Hugo Souza.
NESTORY IRANKUNDA WITH A 𝐖𝐎𝐑𝐋𝐃 𝐂𝐋𝐀𝐒𝐒 FREE KICK AGAINST BRAZIL! 🤯#Socceroos #QLDFootballSeries2026 pic.twitter.com/LkAzbfzuQT
— CommBank Socceroos (@Socceroos) September 25, 2026
No último lance do jogo, Rayan, de cabeça salvou o Brasil da derrota. Raphinha bateu escanteio e o camisa 26 deu boa cabeçada, viu a bola bater em Beach e no travessão antes de entrar no gol para garantir o empate.
Com o Brasil escalado no esquema 4-2-4 mais uma vez, a equipe de Carlo Ancelotti encontrou dificuldades para ter a bola e criar chances de gol contra um adversário inferior. Além disso, as condições do gramado do Estádio Queensland Country Bank, palco do amistoso, receberam críticas nas redes sociais.
O jogo
Jogando literalmente em casa, a Austrália começou acelerando a partida e assustando o Brasil. Logo no primeiro minuto, a equipe de Tony Popovic assustou com chute de Metcalfe e depois em uma recuada errada de Douglas Santos para Hugo Souza.
O goleiro da Amarelinha apareceu pela primeira vez aos 6 minutos de jogo. Irankunda chutou de fora, mas Hugo Souza fez boa defesa e jogou a bola para escanteio. Pouco tempo depois, o arqueiro e Bruno Guimarães se complicaram na saída e Metcalfe voltou a finalizar de longe, mas a defesa bloqueou o chute.
Com dificuldades devido a falta de aproximação entre os setores, o time de Carlo Ancelotti demorou para criar uma boa chance. A primeira saiu com Raphinha, aos 22 minutos, que recebeu lindo lançamento de Danilo e tentou encobrir o goleiro com cabeçada, mas Beach só encaixou sem dificuldades.
Com apenas dois jogadores de meio-campo, o Brasil apostou em lançamentos e ataques em velocidade, com problemas para criar lances coletivos. Aos 34, Hugo Souza fatiou para Estêvão, que achou Vini Jr., mas o camisa 7 finalizou mal a jogada. No melhor momento da equipe, Raphinha e Bruno Guimarães quase abriram o placar, mas faltou eficiência para a dupla.
Antes do fim da primeira etapa, a Austrália voltou a assustar com uma sequência de escanteios.

Falha? Torcida se divide após reação de Hugo Souza no gol da Austrália
Goleira da Seleção Brasileira não pulou após a batida de falta cobrada por Irankunda
O belo gol de falta da Austrália contra o Brasil, marcado por Nestory Irankunda, deu o que falar nas redes sociais. torcedores se dividiram e opinaram sobre a reação do goleiro Hugo Souza no lance.
O ponta australiano cobrou a falta no canto direito de Hugo Souza, mas o goleiro brasileiro apenas fez golpe de vista e não pulou para tentar espalmar a bola. Veja o lance:

artigo.texto: Efforts to Curb Data Center Speculation Gain Ground Across the US Large-load tariffs and other measures to weed out speculative projects are taking shape amid public backlash to data centers and shifting state-level policies. “A fraction of proposed data centers will get built. Utilities are wising up.” That was the headline on a May 2025 Utility Dive article that explored the conundrum speculative data center requests pose for U.S. electric utilities. More than a year later, it’s unclear how much has changed. Community opposition has emerged as a major barrier to data center development, with other challenges including construction labor shortages, long lead times for critical electrical equipment, limited power availability in key markets and uncertainty around consumer demand for artificial intelligence tools. More than $170 billion in AI data center capacity has been “blocked, withdrawn, or stalled” by community opposition since January 2024, the energy advisory company Relae, formerly Carbon Direct, said in June. That’s a sizable chunk of the roughly $581 billion Goldman Sachs expects the big tech companies known as hyperscalers to spend in the U.S. on AI infrastructure, including data center construction, this year. Yet market analysts see no sign that the AI-driven construction boom will disappear anytime soon, despite challenges.

artigo.texto: Google’s Grid-Interactive AI Data Centers: From Backup to Grid Partner At Data Center World Power, Google’s Tom Garvens detailed how full-stack design, LVDC power, BESS, and liquid cooling are reshaping hyperscale AI while supporting local grids. AI infrastructure is expanding at an unprecedented pace. Google now processes more than 3 quadrillion AI tokens per month, representing a sevenfold increase in compute demand from May 2025 to May 2026. Meeting this velocity requires innovation in energy efficiency and power delivery. Tom Garvens, vice president of advanced technology innovation at Google, outlined this challenge during a keynote at Data Center World Power 2026 in Houston, held Sept. 21-23. He described Google’s full-stack approach to scaling AI, positioning data centers as active partners in stabilizing local grids. Turning Backup Power into Grid Services To bridge the speed mismatch between rapid AI rollout and multiyear timelines typical for utility capacity expansion, Google has developed energy strategies that transform backup assets into grid-supportive resources, streamline operations during peak demand, make load shaping more intelligent, and prevent disruptive power swings – while supporting utility resilience. Beyond these strategies, Google is reviewing and redesigning the entire AI data center ecosystem – from chip to utility. This includes optimizing for liquid cooling, low-voltage direct current (LVDC) architectures, intelligent algorithms, and facility design. A core pillar of this work is publishing standardized power and facility technology specifications through communities such as the Open Compute Project (OCP), enabling the industry to build interoperable, efficient, and sustainable infrastructure. “Google has tightly coupled vertical integration in AI along with close partnerships with energy providers,” Garvens said. “We develop and design our own data centers, chips, servers, and rack designs. By having control of our entire hardware and software stack, we can optimize these things together for sustainability and energy efficiency.” Powering AI at Gigawatt Scale Google is investing alongside utilities to add grid capacity. That assistance is vital as a gigawatt-class data center campus can comprise hundreds of thousands of interconnected chips running a single workload. Google’s approach is twofold: work with utility partners to streamline power delivery and adjust its own hardware and software to be more grid-friendly. “Utilities are [setting] different requirements that we must demonstrate that we can meet,” Garvens noted. “Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Nvidia have come together to define an interface spec on how utilities and hyperscalers can interface with each other.” Battery energy storage systems (BESS) have become critical in Google’s campus designs for onsite energy storage and for buffering rapidly fluctuating workloads. Buffering smooths power and voltage transitions. Backup generators remain in use, but diesel does not scale well to campuses at 1 GW and beyond. BESS are increasingly used to provide standby power, supported by demand-response agreements with utilities for peak shaving. “When peak needs are beyond what we've got power for, we can get that from local storage,” Garvens explained. Rather than competing for constrained capacity in saturated markets, Google has been identifying remote sites with ample land and available power. The company is also considering campus developments in small towns where the data center would be a primary employer, he said. Another design change: Google has moved away from centralized Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) systems, favoring rack-level battery backup operating around 54 VDC. Eliminating an extra AC-DC-AC conversion step yields approximately a 1.5% efficiency gain. “We do all of our power conversion at the top of our racks, where we take our AC down to 54 volts, and then we run DC through our racks; our battery backup also runs at that voltage,” Garvens said. Inside the Rack: 54 VDC Today, 800 VDC Tomorrow Google has introduced changes at the chip, rack, and facility levels, supported by software that can intermix workloads to smooth overall load and make it more predictable. Rack density remains a major challenge. Roadmaps anticipate racks approaching 1 MW each over the next year or two. That necessitates liquid cooling for at least the hotter elements within the racks. Delivering the required current at lower voltages would demand bus bars and cabling with significantly more copper. This calls for a higher distribution voltage. Google is pursuing a gradual migration toward 800 VDC for power distribution, which is expected to take a couple of years to mature. In the meantime, Google has implemented “sidecars” alongside its racks – adjacent power-distribution enclosures that house cabling and power gear – reserving the racks for high-density servers. The tradeoff is floor space. When 800 VDC becomes broadly available, those sidecars can be converted to additional AI server racks. “We're working with the industry on bringing solid-state transformers to maturity,” Garvens said. “We are also continuing to improve our power usage effectiveness [PUE]. We can't ever get to 1.0, but we continue to challenge ourselves to get as close to it as possible.” Workload Shifting and Water-Smart Cooling With dozens of data centers in operation and many more in development, Google can be fluid about where it runs workloads. Garvens offered an example: “If there's a heat wave in Ohio and we were running a big workload, we've got agreements in place whereby with the right amount of foresight we can shut certain workloads down or move them elsewhere if they're critical,” he said. “We have a portfolio where we can shift things around.” Water strategy is another focus area. artigo.texto: Patrocinado por: Data center do Google: Brasil fica de fora do radar por enquanto (Google/Reprodução) Repórter de Inteligência Artificial e Tecnologia Publicado em 24 de setembro de 2026 às 12h52. O Google Cloud anunciou que pretende dobrar sua infraestrutura de inteligência artificial agêntica no Brasil até 2030, ampliando capacidade de processamento, armazenamento e computação de alta performance. A empresa afirma que, por enquanto, não planeja novos data centers no país e aposta em infraestrutura de nuvem, GPUs, processamento local de dados e conectividade por cabos submarinos. O Google Cloud anunciou nesta quinta-feira, 24, que pretende dobrar a infraestrutura para o desenvolvimento de inteligência artificial (IA) agêntica no Brasil até 2030 — mas que, ao menos por enquanto, não vai apostar em data centers. Em coletiva de imprensa durante o Google Cloud Summit Brasil, em São Paulo, da qual a EXAME participou, Eduardo López, presidente do Google Cloud para a América Latina, afirmou que "todo investimento tem a ver com demanda". "Nossa aposta de crescimento na demanda das empresas brasileiras é no uso corporativo da IA. Os data centers são importantes. Vamos duplicar nossa capacidade no Brasil", disse. "Como isso vai acontecer, é um serviço de demanda de mercado — e não tanto sobre data centers." Nos próximos quatro anos, a empresa irá aumentar a capacidade local de processamento, armazenamento e computação de alta performance para IA. Na prática, o anúncio se traduz em três frentes. A primeira é o processamento local de dados: a partir de 15 de outubro, a versão web do Gemini Enterprise, plataforma corporativa de agentes de IA da empresa, passa a processar dentro do Brasil os dados de clientes que usam o modelo Gemini 3.5 Flash — mudança que se soma ao armazenamento local já existente para fluxos de trabalho de agentes, e que busca atender exigências regulatórias e de soberania de dados no país. O Google Cloud reforça que, em qualquer região, os dados e resultados dos clientes não são usados para treinar os modelos da empresa sem consentimento explícito. De volta ao topo: como o Google virou o jogo na corrida da IA A segunda é o hardware: máquinas virtuais equipadas com GPUs Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition já estão disponíveis na região de nuvem de São Paulo, voltadas a cargas de trabalho de inferência pesada e em tempo real. A terceira, segundo López, são os cabos submarinos, que ele apresentou como prioridade tão importante quanto os próprios data centers. "Quando vocês falam de infraestrutura, quando vocês falam de soluções, são duas variáveis muito importantes: os data centers e a conectividade. A conectividade é muito importante", disse. "Nós vamos às duas coisas sempre." O detalhe técnico por trás dessa escolha, segundo López, é que a localização de um data center do Google costuma seguir a rota dos cabos submarinos da empresa, e não o contrário — o que ajuda a explicar por que a companhia tem historicamente concentrado seus investimentos em cabos que ligam o Brasil aos Estados Unidos via São Paulo, e não em novas cidades. "Não usamos nossos cabos para começar os data centers; temos um problema de latência se estiver fora da região", afirmou. Questionado sobre o que torna o Brasil um destino tão relevante para a empresa, o presidente global do Google Cloud, Thomas Kurian, disse que os investimentos "são um reflexo de uma resposta à demanda dos nossos clientes" e da "evolução do mercado" brasileiro, um dos mais relevantes da América Latina em adoção tecnológica. Para Milton Larsen Burgese, diretor do Setor Público do Google Cloud para a América Latina, o "jeitinho brasileiro" tem a ver com a decisão. "O brasileiro adora tecnologia, então eu acho que é uma somatória de fatores que estão acontecendo que levam o Brasil a passar especial em relação a esses investimentos", disse. A América Latina é hoje a segunda região que mais cresce para o Google Cloud no mundo, com o Brasil como o país mais importante dentro dela. Para López, a educação é a parte central dessa estratégia. A empresa já treinou 3 milhões de brasileiros em tecnologias de nuvem e IA — meta que havia começado em 1 milhão e foi ampliada em junho —, em parceria com 140 universidades no país. Questionado se o investimento anunciado deve resultar em um novo cabo submarino chegando a Fortaleza, hoje um dos principais hubs de conectividade do país ao lado de Salvador, Rio de Janeiro e Santos, López não confirmou nem descartou a possibilidade — e reafirmou que decisões desse tipo costumam ser tomadas em nível global pela empresa, considerando a proximidade com data centers existentes — a maioria deles, hoje, próxima a São Paulo. O anúncio chega num momento de forte expansão do setor de data centers no Brasil como um todo: o país recebeu 106 megawatts de nova capacidade só no primeiro semestre de 2026 e pode somar mais 134 megawatts até dezembro, segundo o relatório Data Center Brasil 2026, da consultoria JLL, que projeta cerca de US$ 8 bilhões em investimentos no setor neste ano. Hoje, o Google opera 30 data centers ativos em 11 países, além de outras unidades em fase de construção, segundo o próprio mapa da empresa. A maior concentração está na América do Norte, principalmente nos Estados Unidos, seguida pela Europa, com unidades em países como Irlanda, Holanda, Alemanha, Finlândia e Bélgica, e pela Ásia, com data centers no Japão, em Taiwan e em Cingapura. Na América do Sul, porém, a empresa opera apenas duas unidades: uma no Uruguai, em Canelones, e outra no Chile, em Quilicura, perto de Santiago. Por enquanto, não. Segundo Eduardo López, presidente do Google Cloud para a América Latina, a empresa pretende aumentar a capacidade de infraestrutura de IA no Brasil sem anunciar novos data centers. O foco será ampliar processamento, armazenamento e computação de alta performance conforme a demanda dos clientes. Set us as preferred For more than three days, fire crews have worked to address a lithium-ion battery fire in La Verne that has forced the evacuation of hundreds of residents and raised questions about the safety of California’s rapidly expanding energy storage systems. The state has invested heavily in battery storage — which holds on to energy captured by solar panels during the day so it can be used when electricity demand peaks in the evening — as it pushes to meet its ambitious goal of 100% clean-energy usage by 2045. But these sites also come with dangers, as demonstrated by the massive Moss Landing battery fire in January 2025, which prompted the evacuation of about 1,500 residents and deposited heavy metals in a nearby estuary. The La Verne battery fire is much smaller in scale but nonetheless alarming for those who had to leave their homes or deal with the closure of schools due to the potential of hazardous fumes. “It’s really disheartening that our schoolchildren continue to be put at risk like this over and over,” said Assemblymember Dawn Addis (D-Morro Bay), who pushed for stricter safety regulations around battery storage in the aftermath of the Moss Landing fire. The La Verne blaze began shortly before noon Tuesday inside one of four 250-kilowatt-battery containers at the Metropolitan Water District’s facility on Wheeler Avenue, according to the La Verne Fire Department. As crews successfully stabilized the initial container, an adjacent 250-kilowatt container then started to overheat. The facility’s battery storage system, which was brought on line in June, stores energy captured at the water treatment plant’s solar farm. Battery fires are challenging to combat because, when a battery is damaged, a self-sustaining chemical reaction called thermal runaway can occur and easily spread to adjacent batteries. Your morning catch-up: Battery power in California, wildfires trigger unhealthful air quality alert in SoCal and more big stories When thermal runaway starts, the process can continue for days, with the potential for batteries to release toxic gases such as hydrogen fluoride, hydrogen chloride and carbon monoxide. In La Verne, air quality monitoring had not detected any hazardous emissions Thursday, but the unstable nature of the batteries and potential risk of toxic fumes led officials to keep evacuations in place in the immediate area around the site, Fire Department Battalion Chief Mark Savage said. Crews were able to stabilize the temperature of the second storage box by Thursday afternoon, enabling first responders to begin the process of de-energizing the individual batteries, with the hope of resolving the incident soon and enabling investigators to begin probing the cause of the fire. On Friday morning, La Verne police officials announced the batteries had been removed and evacuation orders were lifted and residents could return to their homes. A local elementary school remained closed, however. The fire would be discussed in further detail by the City Council on Tuesday. The La Verne fire comes just days after another battery fire erupted at Moss Landing, reigniting concerns at one of the state’s largest battery storage sites. About 55,000 batteries were damaged in the initial incident, the cause of which remains under investigation. Batteries connected to the grid are essential for addressing climate change, but some neighbors worry about hard-to-extinguish fires The initial Moss Landing fire sparked a flurry oflegislative proposals to bolster California’s energy storage safety. State Senate Bill 283, authored by Sen. John Laird (D-Santa Cruz), was signed into law in October and requires battery storage developers to consult with local fire authorities and undergo fire inspection before going on line. It also requires that they adhere to safety standards established by the National Fire Protection Assn. Other proposals that would have created stricter requirements around the approval process for new storage sites did not advance through the Legislature this session. They include Assembly Bill 303, which would have required local authorities to be part of the permitting process for facilities and would have established a 3,200-foot setback requirement from sensitive areas such as schools, homes, hospitals and environmentally sensitive habitat. Bill author Addis said she was disappointed the bill never received a committee hearing, and plans on reintroducing new safety legislation in the next legislative cycle. “We do need to transition off of oil and gas,” she said. “And as we transition, we cannot keep making these mistakes and treating people really with the disrespect that dirty energy has treated our communities with.” Independent of the Legislature, the California Public Utilities Commission, the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection and the California Energy Commission have made regulatory changes around battery energy storage sites in recent years. Best practices around battery storage, and the technology of batteries themselves, have improved since the Moss Landing storage facility began construction in 2020. New large-scale facilities typically use more stable lithium-iron-phosphate batteries that are stored in outdoor containers configured to limit the spread of a potential fire, according to the California Energy Commission. They are also subject to more robust testing and emergency response requirements. Most of these improvements have focused on larger utility-scale storage sites such as Moss Landing. artigo.texto: Os sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias podem reduzir entre 40% e 50% os cortes de geração no sistema elétrico brasileiro, segundo estimativa do diretor-geral do Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS), Márcio Rea. O percentual dependerá do resultado do leilão de reserva de capacidade de baterias previsto para dezembro. “A bateria vai ajudar muito. Até na questão do curtailment, se eu calculo entre 40% e 50%, deve melhorar, deve diminuir”, afirmou Rea durante o CNN Talks Energia, realizado nesta quinta-feira, 24 de setembro. O armazenamento é uma das ferramentas avaliadas pelo ONS para lidar com a mudança do perfil de operação provocada pelo crescimento da geração solar. “Há dias, como na semana passada, em que a gente teve 38% de energia solar no Brasil, maior do que a hidráulica, que foi 33%. Neste dia, a gente tinha uma rampa de duas Itaipus e meia de potência. Você imagina a dificuldade de administrar, das duas horas da tarde até as 18h, 19h, essa rampa”, afirmou Rea. Rea afirmou que o leilão de reserva de capacidade já realizado chegou em um momento necessário, mas que o sistema ainda precisa de mais recursos. Além das baterias, citou as usinas hidrelétricas reversíveis como alternativa para ampliar a flexibilidade e reduzir os cortes de geração. O diretor-geral ponderou que o curtailment não será eliminado e que o problema também ocorre em outros sistemas elétricos com elevada participação de fontes renováveis. Custeio O modelo de custeio das baterias, porém, ainda provoca questionamentos entre geradores. O diretor-executivo de Marketing, Comercialização e Novos Negócios da Eneva, Marcelo Lopes, criticou a possibilidade de térmicas e hidrelétricas também arcarem com os custos da contratação. “Ninguém entende como razoável que o gerador que é a solução seja o responsável por pagar uma conta”, afirmou. Segundo Lopes, não seria razoável que térmicas e hidrelétricas arcassem com o custo. Ele evitou antecipar uma eventual judicialização caso o desenho seja mantido e disse acreditar que o tema será “devidamente endereçado” pelo poder concedente e pela Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel). O secretário-executivo do Ministério de Minas e Energia (MME), Gustavo Cerqueira Ataíde, afirmou que a expectativa do governo para o leilão é positiva e que o volume de projetos cadastrados mostrou forte interesse do mercado. Segundo ele, as baterias são consideradas promissoras não apenas para o fornecimento de potência, objetivo da contratação prevista para dezembro, mas também para outras aplicações no sistema elétrico. Ataíde acrescentou que os critérios de segurança do suprimento estão evoluindo para incorporar a flexibilidade, além de energia e potência. Sinal de preço O CEO da PSR, Luiz Augusto Barroso, afirmou que os cortes de geração passarão a fazer parte da operação do sistema brasileiro e que a regulação precisa criar mecanismos para lidar com o problema. Para Barroso, não faz sentido cortar geração em momentos de excesso de oferta e manter o preço da energia acima de zero. “Em outros países ele é até negativo”, disse. Segundo ele, um preço igual a zero nesses períodos reduz o custo econômico do corte ao tornar indiferente, para o gerador, produzir energia ou adquiri-la no mercado de curto prazo. Ataíde também apontou problemas no sinal de preço. Segundo o secretário-executivo, o piso atual do Preço de Liquidação das Diferenças (PLD), que impede que o valor chegue a zero, produz um sinal inadequado em situações de excesso de geração. O MME já colocou o tema em discussão na Consulta Pública 228/2026, que trata da revisão do Decreto 5.163/2004. Entre as mudanças propostas estão novos critérios para a definição dos limites mínimo e máximo do PLD. Na nota técnica que embasa a consulta, o ministério avalia que o atual piso do preço, influenciado pelos custos de Itaipu, dificulta a sinalização econômica nos períodos de excesso de geração.

artigo.texto: A WEG anunciou nesta sexta-feira, 25 de setembro, a ampliação do projeto de sua nova fábrica de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS), em construção na cidade de Itajaí, em Santa Catarina. Com a revisão, o investimento total estimado no projeto chega a R$ 330 milhões, enquanto a capacidade produtiva será ampliada para 4 GWh por ano. O início das operações está previsto para o segundo semestre de 2027. Anunciada em fevereiro deste ano, a unidade foi projetada para atender à demanda por soluções de armazenamento de energia associadas à transição energética e tinha, inicialmente, financiamento de R$ 280 milhões do programa BNDES Mais Inovação, em parceria com a Finep. Na época, a WEG informou que a nova fábrica deveria gerar cerca de 90 empregos diretos e amplie a capacidade produtiva da empresa em sistemas BESS para até 2 GWh por ano, volume equivalente a cerca de 400 sistemas com capacidade de 5 MWh cada. Em comunicado, a empresa informou que a ampliação incorpora maior nível de automação e ganhos de eficiência industrial, permitindo elevar a capacidade produtiva da fábrica. Para a companhia, a planta reforça a sua estratégia de acompanhar o crescimento do mercado de armazenamento de energia no Brasil, especialmente diante da realização do primeiro Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade na forma de Potência para Armazenamento Nacional, previsto para 2 dezembro de 2026. A WEG está entre as sete empresas credenciadas pelo Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) como fornecedoras de sistemas de armazenamento de energia no processo criado para o certame “O mercado de armazenamento de energia vive um momento de forte expansão, impulsionado pelo crescimento das fontes renováveis e pela necessidade crescente de maior flexibilidade e segurança para o sistema elétrico. A ampliação deste projeto demonstra a capacidade da WEG de adaptar rapidamente seus investimentos para atender às necessidades do mercado e apoiar o desenvolvimento sustentável do setor energético brasileiro”, afirmou Manfred Peter Johann, vice-presidente de Automação e Sistemas da WEG. O complexo também incluirá um laboratório dedicado a testes, desenvolvimento e qualificação de produtos, com foco em aprimoramento de processos e aceleração da inovação em soluções de armazenamento. A infraestrutura prevê ainda uma subestação própria para simular condições reais de operação dos sistemas, permitindo validar desempenho e segurança dos equipamentos. O investimento da empresa ocorre em meio ao avanço da geração renovável, especialmente solar e eólica, que aumenta a demanda por soluções de flexibilidade e confiabilidade do sistema elétrico. Os sistemas de armazenamento permitem acumular energia em períodos de baixa demanda e liberá-la nos momentos de maior consumo ou menor geração, contribuindo para reduzir riscos operacionais e oscilações na rede.

A tecnologia ajuda a reduzir os cortes de geração, conhecidos como curtailment, e oferece maior flexibilidade e segurança à operação do sistema elétrico. artigo.texto: Por: Bianca Wolf, Marvin Menezes e Patricia Dayrell* Em menos de dois anos, os data centers deixaram de ser uma pauta restrita ao setor de tecnologia para ocupar posição central na agenda energética brasileira. O tema passou a mobilizar o governo federal, o Ministério de Minas e Energia (MME), a Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel), o Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS) e os agentes do setor elétrico diante de uma questão que, embora nova para a economia digital, é bastante conhecida pelos profissionais de energia: a disputa por acesso à infraestrutura de transmissão. O movimento não ocorreu por acaso. Impulsionado pela expansão da inteligência artificial (IA), da computação em nuvem e da crescente demanda por processamento de dados, o Brasil passou a ser visto como um destino particularmente atrativo para a instalação de grandes centros de dados. A combinação entre uma matriz elétrica predominantemente renovável e barata, e a disponibilidade de recursos energéticos para expansão, aliada à proximidade dos grandes centros de consumo de dados, colocou o país no radar de investidores nacionais e estrangeiros. Os números ajudam a explicar a dimensão do fenômeno. Segundo dados divulgados pelo ONS, dos 43 pedidos de acesso recentemente formalizados para conexão à rede básica, 38 estavam relacionados a projetos de data centers, que, sozinhos, representavam aproximadamente 7.040 MW de carga requerida ao Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN). Para fins de comparação, esse montante supera a demanda máxima de diversas capitais brasileiras e se aproxima da carga total de alguns estados. A concentração geográfica também é expressiva. Apenas o estado de São Paulo concentrava 20 solicitações de acesso, correspondentes a cerca de 3.914 MW de demanda. Os números evidenciam que a expansão da infraestrutura digital deixou de representar um fenômeno pontual para se tornar um fator relevante no planejamento da expansão da rede elétrica brasileira. Esse rápido aumento da disputa por pontos de conexão à rede de transmissão ocorreu justamente no momento em que o setor elétrico passou a enxergar paralelos com experiências recentes vividas durante o período de expansão das fontes renováveis. Esse cenário trouxe à memória discussões já conhecidas pelo setor elétrico brasileiro. Ao longo dos últimos anos, especialmente durante o período de expansão das fontes renováveis, o país assistiu à multiplicação de pedidos de acesso à rede de transmissão e à crescente disputa por capacidade de conexão em regiões com elevado potencial para implantação de novos empreendimentos. Em muitos casos, os pedidos foram apresentados em estágios ainda incipientes na maturidade dos projetos, levando à ocupação de capacidade da rede por empreendimentos que posteriormente foram considerados inviáveis de serem implantados, seja por não terem obtido financiamento, não avançado nos processos de licenciamento ou por outros motivos [1]. Naturalmente, a perspectiva de dezenas de novos empreendimentos disputando acesso à rede básica despertou preocupações semelhantes. Afinal, como garantir que a capacidade disponível da rede seja efetivamente destinada a projetos viáveis? Como evitar a reserva antecipada de capacidade por empreendimentos ainda incertos? E como compatibilizar a expansão de grandes cargas com o planejamento da infraestrutura necessária para atendê-las? Foi nesse contexto que o governo federal editou o Decreto nº 12.772, de 5 de dezembro de 2025, instituindo a Política Nacional de Acesso ao Sistema de Transmissão (Pnast). Embora sua aplicação não se restrinja aos data centers, a política surge em um período marcado pela intensificação das disputas por acesso à rede básica e pela necessidade de racionalizar a utilização da capacidade disponível do sistema. A nova política promove uma profunda reformulação dos procedimentos de acesso à transmissão ao introduzir instrumentos como as Temporadas de Acesso, processos competitivos e mecanismos voltados à coordenação entre a expansão da rede e a ocupação da capacidade existente. Paralelamente às discussões sobre acesso à transmissão, o governo passou a estruturar iniciativas destinadas à atração de investimentos em infraestrutura digital com o objetivo de posicionar o Brasil como um polo global de infraestrutura digital. Dessa forma, foi publicada a Medida Provisória nº 1.318/2025, que instituiu o Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Data Center (Redata), prevendo incentivos fiscais para empreendimentos do setor condicionados ao cumprimento de determinados requisitos de sustentabilidade e investimento. Apesar da relevância atribuída à iniciativa, a Medida Provisória não foi convertida em lei dentro do prazo constitucional, perdendo sua eficácia em fevereiro de 2026. A caducidade do Redata, contudo, não encerrou o debate. Poucos dias depois, foi apresentado o Projeto de Lei nº 278/2026, que retomava substancialmente o mesmo modelo de incentivos fiscais previsto na Medida Provisória. A iniciativa evidenciava a persistência do entendimento de que a atração de data centers deveria constituir um objetivo estratégico da política econômica nacional. Enquanto o Redata estava centrado na concessão de incentivos tributários, a nova proposta passa a tratar os data centers como infraestrutura estratégica para o desenvolvimento nacional. Entre outras medidas, o projeto prevê prioridade de acesso às redes de transmissão em regiões com excedente de geração, aproximando definitivamente a política de desenvolvimento dos data centers das discussões relacionadas ao planejamento do setor elétrico. A sucessão desses movimentos revela que a expansão dos data centers passou a ser analisada sob múltiplas perspectivas. Se, por um lado, o governo federal tem ressaltado o potencial estratégico desses empreendimentos para posicionar o Brasil como um polo global de infraestrutura digital, por outro, a crescente concentração de pedidos de acesso à rede básica trouxe para o centro do debate questõe

artigo.texto: WEG amplia aportes e capacidade produtiva prevista para nova fábrica de baterias em SC A WEG ampliou o projeto de sua nova fábrica de baterias (BESS) em Itajaí (SC), elevando o investimento previsto de R$ 280 milhões para R$ 330 milhões. A unidade, que iniciará as operações no segundo semestre de 2027, terá a capacidade anual dobrada para 4 GWh para atender à crescente demanda da transição energética. O anúncio ocorre às vésperas do primeiro leilão de baterias do sistema elétrico nacional, marcado para dezembro, que contará com concorrência exclusiva para projetos de conteúdo local. A WEG anunciou nesta sexta-feira uma ampliação do projeto de uma nova fábrica de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) em construção em Itajaí (SC), aumentando sua expectativa de investimentos e capacidade produtiva na unidade. Segundo a companhia, a nova fábrica terá um investimento total estimado de R$330 milhões e capacidade anual de 4 gigawatts-hora (GWh), "atendendo à demanda crescente por soluções associadas à transição energética, com início das operações previsto para o segundo semestre de 2027". Em fevereiro, na ocasião do primeiro anúncio sobre o projeto, a WEG havia estimado uma capacidade de até 2 GWh ao ano e citado um financiamento de R$280 milhões. A ampliação do empreendimento ocorre no contexto do primeiro leilão para contratação de baterias para o sistema elétrico brasileiro, programado para dezembro. A licitação terá uma concorrência específica para projetos com conteúdo nacional, após ampla mobilização da indústria brasileira do segmento.

artigo.texto: BUDAPEST, Hungary, Sept. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hoymiles has launched the HoyUltra 2000M, its full-scenario commercial and industrial (C&I) battery energy storage system (BESS), at the first stop of its European C&I Energy Storage Roadshow in Budapest on 24th-25th September 2026. The roadshow takes Hoymiles' C&I storage portfolio and project experience to local developers, investors and partners across Europe. Europe's C&I energy storage market is entering a more project-driven stage, where opportunities increasingly depend not only on technology, but also on project economics, safety, certification and execution. In this context, Hoymiles takes its C&I BESS expertise directly to local markets through a European roadshow tour, presenting how its new HoyUltra 2000M makes a difference for businesses. Co-organized with GNX, the Budapest roadshow covered European storage market trends, C&I business opportunities, certification, project development and operational returns. "By partnering with Hoymiles, we bring together technology and local market experience to help European customers explore practical opportunities in C&I energy storage", said GNX CEO Daniel Racsek. Experts from S&P Global Commodity Insights, LCP Delta and TÜV SÜD shared perspectives on market trends, business models, European standards and safety requirements. In a keynote presentation, Susanne von Aichberger, Principal Analyst at S&P Global Commodity Insights, described C&I BESS as "a market coming of age". Overall, BESS is transforming from an emerging market to a critical infrastructure. The HoyUltra 2000M is a full-scenario C&I energy storage solution for applications from small commercial systems to large-scale projects. The platform already covers small, mid-size and large C&I use cases, with more than 2 GWh of Hoymiles C&I storage in operation worldwide. "As the European C&I market evolves, customers need more than individual products. They need solutions that can address different project scenarios and the realities of deployment," said Guy Rong, Hoymiles Vice President. On the following day, participants visited a local C&I solar-plus-storage project in Hungary, where 16 HoyUltra 2000M systems were deployed. It reflects the company's ambition to deepen its presence in Europe's C&I energy storage market and work more closely with local partners throughout the project lifecycle. Following Budapest, the roadshow will continue across multiple European cities, bringing Hoymiles' full-scenario C&I energy storage solutions and local market engagement to more customers and partners. artigo.texto: Talk of a new AI data center is stirring in the small town of Morrison, Oklahoma, and surrounding communities as residents grapple with the fear of the unknown. “We don’t know what kind of energy these things are going to put out to the people who live around it,” said Adam Ingram, a former resident of Noble County. “We don’t know what kind of bad transmissions go outside of the building and what it does to nature.” Comstock Holdings Companies Inc. announced a joint venture with Jericho Energy Ventures Inc. for the development of “large-scale data center campuses in Oklahoma's Pawnee and Noble counties” on June 6. With little to no public information, residents are expressing concerns online about what changes the Black Bear data center campus will bring. Neither Jericho nor Comstock responded in time for comment before publication. Ingram, who no longer lives in Noble County but owns 160 acres of land and has family in the area, wonders what the environmental impacts will be. Additionally, Ingram worries the expected light and noise pollution could result in a lifestyle change for the rural community. “It would be a total environmental change for just the way of life out there if you can’t go outside and see the stars and really be in the country,” Ingram said. “That would be really upsetting to me personally. “Maybe that doesn’t affect the environmental [pollution] side of things… but if you light that [data center] up all night, that will be like a city right in your backyard.” Ingram said he supports the right to purchase, sell and develop land as an individual desires; however, he questions the ethics of those developments when it can negatively impact the surrounding land and people. In 2025, rep. Amanda Clinton of Tulsa, Oklahoma, ordered an interim study on the impact of data center expansion on Oklahoma’s water resources and power grid in front of the Utilities Committee. Ingram would like the results of this study to be analyzed and released before Oklahoma legislators and leaders allow large-scale developments of data centers. Additionally, he thinks the federal government should step in to lead these studies and leave it up to the states for interpretation and decision making. Although Ingram is worrisome of the environmental impacts, he said he understands the financial gain communities with data centers see. With a proper understanding of data centers, the impacts and solutions to known issues, he believes he could support the development of one. “[The tax revenue] could be a huge benefit to the local community,” Ingram said. “If it’s done right, and I’m talking correctly because then there’s nothing to protest. It’s like putting in a blue-collar factory.” Similar to Ingram, Sarah Mautino, a long-time resident of Pawnee County, believes the development of data centers without understanding the impacts is worrisome. Mautino, who inherited her family’s farm and home in Pawnee County, said she cares deeply about preserving the land for herself and future family members. For Mautino, the unknown impacts on local bodies of water are her biggest concerns. “People in rural Oklahoma understand how precious water is and how quickly a drought can change everything,” Mautino said. “I want to know where the water will come from, how much will actually be used and what that could mean for our wells, farms, livestock, creeks and families.” Additionally, Mautino is concerned about the environmental impacts such as air, noise and light pollution; wildlife disruption; and the loss of agricultural and hunting land. The 44-year-old said she understands why the development of Black Bear data center campus is enticing to both local and state leaders, noting the job opportunities and potential tax revenue. However, Mautino wants to see numbers, facts and data showing the benefits. “How many permanent jobs will there be,” Mautino said. “Will they go to local people? What incentives are being offered? Who will pay for road repairs, expanded utilities and additional fire and emergency services? “The community deserves to know whether the benefits truly match what we’re being asked to give up.” Like Ingram, Mautino believes local and state leaders should slow down development until more long-term effects of data centers are understood. A public records request from both Noble and Pawnee County clerks showed no sign of land purchases by either Jericho or Comstock. However, on Monday a user by the name Dylan James, emailed both Noble and Pawnee County commissioners offices requesting full transparency on the Black Bear Campus Data Center before any governing decisions are made. An excerpt from the email reads, “Before Noble County takes any additional zoning, land-use, road, infrastructure, incentive or other discretionary action concerning this project, I am asking the Board to ensure that residents receive a complete accounting of what is proposed and what approvals remain outstanding.” The Black Bear campus Although a map has not been released of the location, Jericho referred to the campus as being “strategically placed” 20 minutes West of the Google Data Center in Stillwater and 45 Minutes East of Meta’s in Tulsa. Phase one of the hyperscale project would include a 400-acre platform, expected to expand to 10,000 acres. Although no records were pulled indicating either Jericho or Comstock own land, a filing from the U.S. Security and Exchange Commission indicates Jericho has secured at least 20 lease agreements with residents in North Central Oklahoma. The total acreage among these lease agreements surpasses 6,000. Additionally, Jericho projects the facility to operate with a 20-mw grid capacity in phase one. However, the power usage is expected to reach a 2,646-mw capacity by 2032. Jericho states it will have a 345 kV transmission for onsite power operations. However, it is unclear how much of the estimated power consumption will come from the transmission or the grid. Jericho also states it will

artigo.texto: Democrat gubernatorial candidate Cindy Holscher spent much of the past weekend in Emporia. Holscher visited with constituents at Gravel City Roasters on Saturday, following that appearance with an educator meet-and-greet at the Lyon County Democrat party headquarters Sunday. Following the meet-and-greet Sunday, and with lawmakers likely looking at possible changes to the state’s public education funding mechanism in the 2027 session, Holscher says the current formula is effective — but the state’s policy on underfunding special education is not. Holscher says that decision to underfund special education rolls into the longstanding debate into how to adjust property tax policy and give residents some relief. Holscher says the Legislature’s most important job is to fund public schools, not develop tax breaks for rich people. The one issue that has rapidly overtaken property tax adjustments is data centers, and Holscher — who is running against Republican Ty Masterson for the chance to succeed Democrat Governor Laura Kelly — has called for a moratorium on data center policy matters. She wants to see more guardrails, more state-level protections and more guarantees about local jobs before potential projects go forward. Holscher also tells KVOE News local communities are seeking guidance from the state as potential data center projects, including one in Emporia, continue to generate heated debate. Political appearances continue this week. Kansas Attorney General candidate Chris Mann, the Democrat facing off against Republican incumbent Kris Kobach, has a fundraiser in Emporia from 5:30-7 pm Monday. The location has not been divulged. US House Second District candidate Don Coover, a Democrat running against incumbent Republican Derek Schmidt, will stop at the Reading Community Center from 6-7:30 pm Tuesday.

artigo.texto: Council approves second reading on one-year data center moratorium Jasper County Council passed second reading on a one-year moratorium for data centers in the unincorporated areas of Jasper County. Third reading will be held at the next council meeting. - Jasper County Council is considering a one-year moratorium on new data centers in unincorporated areas. - Officials have cited concerns over the large amounts of water and electricity required by data centers. - The moratorium would allow staff time to study the impacts and develop regulations for these facilities. - During a public hearing, residents and conservation groups spoke in support of the temporary ban. Jasper County Council is working to ensure that the appropriate steps are being taken before it would even consider accepting any future requests from data centers that seek to locate in the unincorporated areas of the county. Council, during its Sept. 21 meeting, unanimously approved the second reading of an ordinance for a one-year moratorium on the centers in unincorporated Jasper County. This ordinance also allows council, if needed, to extend the moratorium for a period of six months at a time. A third and final reading of the ordinance will be required and will take place at the next Jasper County Council meeting. The Sept. 8 approval or first reading of the pending ordinance doctrine gave the county authority to enforce the requirements which are outlined in the ordinance before final reading. Data centers have been topics of numerous discussions among county councils across the Lowcountry as other councils are also considering moratoriums. Leaders have cited concerns over the amount of water and electricity which could be required by the centers. A data center is a facility that houses Information Technology (IT) infrastructure which includes servers, storage systems and networking equipment which stores processes and manages digital data. The centers, according to officials, can significantly increase both electricity and water demand, consuming millions of gallons of water annually and placing a strain on local power grids. Jasper County Director of Planning and Building Services brought the ordinance before council for second reading, explaining staff felt as though a one-year moratorium was needed. “With the increased number of data centers seeking to locate to South Carolina, staff believes it is necessary to ask county council to place a temporary moratorium on the acceptance of any applications for rezoning, site plans, building permits and any type of economic incentives for data centers, data processing facilities, crypto mining operations and any other uses associated with data processing facilities within unincorporated Jasper County,” Wagner said. The moratorium, Wagner said, is proposed for one year and would allow staff time to review and make sure there are adequate provisions with the Jasper County Zoning Ordinance and land development regulations to control the location the design, the size, density, land use, and infrastructure needs for data centers and data processing facilities and cryptocurrency mining operations. “The planning staff intends to have an ordinance regulating data centers, data processing facilities, and crypto mining operations ready for adoption by the time the moratorium expires,” Wagner said. Staff’s plan, Wagner said, includes considering and planning for the potential impacts of data center development, learn how much water and power usage is necessary to support these uses, ensure the county has plans and policies to ensure that the data center development is consistent with the county’s development objectives and that potential negative impacts are prevented or mitigated. The plan, Wagner said, would also identify appropriate locations for data centers within the county, ensuring these locations are identified in the county’s comprehensive plan and permitted by the county zoning and land use ordinances. The plan would also recommend clear standards for data center development within the county. “Article Six of the Jasper County Zoning Ordinance use regulation utilizes the North American Industry Classification System (also known as the NAICS Code), as the basis for determining the use of a property,” Wagner said. “Currently, the NAICS Code within that use table would allow data centers as a use by right in the community commercial, general commercial, industrial development and the mixed business zoning districts.” Wagner said the ordinance was reviewed by the Jasper County Planning Commission during its Aug. 11 meeting and they recommended approval of the one-year ordinance for a moratorium. “This ordinance does invoke the pending ordinance doctrine,” Wagner said. Public hearing held Two people appeared before council during the public hearing to discuss their thoughts about the moratorium with council. Both said they were in support of the one-year moratorium, and no one spoke against the moratorium. “I applaud the council’s vision and wisdom as you consider the proposed one-year moratorium on data processing centers,” Ridgeland resident Nancy Lowther said. “I believe that this time will allow you, as our county leaders, to see the impact that data center construction and operations have on our neighboring counties in which they have already been approved.” Lowther also said she believed the county’s facilities and infrastructure were overburdened with projects already underway. “Even with financial incentives, I believe it would be a mistake to move forward with one of these projects at this time,” Lowther said. Coastal Conservation League South Coast Office Director Grant McClure also commended council for moving forward with a one-year moratorium. “I’m here tonight to express support for the proposed moratorium on data centers in Jasper County,” McClure said. “We are seeing these facilities pop up all across South Carolina and also in Georgia in places like Effingham Cou

Visitors can meet the leagend team at Booth V7315, Venetian Expo, Level 2, where the company will present its SuperCap Jump Starter Series, professional battery testers, battery monitors, smart battery chargers and thermal imaging solutions. One of leagend's latest R&D developments, the new leagend SuperCap Battery, will also be on display for visitors to experience at the show. For automotive aftermarket distributors, importers, battery and parts businesses, tool suppliers, service networks, fleet operators and automotive brands, AAPEX provides an opportunity to see how these technologies can fit different vehicle applications and market needs while discussing distribution, private-label and OEM/ODM cooperation with the leagend team. Battery-Free Starting Support Built to Stay with the Vehicle Conventional portable jump starters provide emergency starting assistance, but they depend on an internal battery that must be kept sufficiently charged before it is needed. The leagend SuperCap Jump Starter Series uses supercapacitor technology instead of an internal chemical battery and is designed to remain installed on the vehicle. Once installed, the system functions as on-board starting support rather than a portable booster that must be located and connected after a no-start occurs. Its low-power design allows it to remain connected for long periods, while the battery-free architecture removes the need to periodically recharge an internal lithium battery. The leagend SuperCap Jump Starter Series also incorporates AI self-learning, driving and forced-start modes. Through the companion smart app, users can view battery condition, operating status, starting records and alerts. These functions combine starting assistance with ongoing visibility into vehicle starting behavior rather than limiting the product to one-time emergency use. For workshops, the system can be installed as part of vehicle service. For fleet operators and commercial vehicle users, having starting support already installed on the vehicle can reduce reliance on separately stored portable boosters when additional starting assistance is required. As temperature falls, a starting battery has less available power, while a cold engine can require more current to crank. A battery that is able to start a vehicle under normal conditions may therefore be unable to provide sufficient starting power in low-temperature environments. Battery-based portable jump starters can face similar limitations because low temperatures can reduce the available output of their internal batteries. Their readiness also depends on the charge remaining in the booster when starting assistance is required. The leagend SuperCap Jump Starter Series is designed to operate from -40Â°C to 80Â°C. Its supercapacitor architecture provides stable high-current output in low-temperature environments without relying on an internal booster battery. When the vehicle's starting battery is too weak to complete a normal start, the installed JS unit can provide additional starting support. This operating range is particularly relevant for vehicles used in regions with severe winters or large seasonal temperature changes. For fleets and commercial vehicle operators, it provides an additional means of addressing winter no-start situations without depending solely on a separately stored battery booster. For workshops and distributors, it provides a starting-support option for customers whose vehicles regularly operate under low-temperature conditions. The product family covers different vehicle applications. The leagend JS200, leagend JS300 and leagend JS400 address different 12V passenger-vehicle and SUV starting requirements, while the leagend JS600 extends the SuperCap concept to 24V commercial vehicles, diesel vehicles and heavy equipment. Professional Battery Testing That Supports Better Service Decisions Starting assistance solves one part of a battery problem. Understanding the condition of the battery and electrical system is another, particularly for workshops and battery businesses that need to decide whether a battery should be maintained, replaced or investigated further. leagend battery testers are built around the company's battery testing technologies and algorithms, with high-precision testing for different battery systems and service environments. The leagend BA4000 offers broad application coverage, supporting 6V, 12V and 24V lead-acid starting batteries together with vehicle cranking and charging-system tests. Its built-in printer and test-record functions make the results useful beyond the diagnostic screen. A workshop or battery dealer can provide customers with a printed test result, retain a service record or document battery condition for replacement and after-sales cases. For businesses focused on 12V and 24V systems, the leagend BA2000 provides a more focused professional option with printed reporting. Other leagend battery testers address different battery types and levels of diagnostic demand, giving distributors and tool suppliers flexibility to match products to different workshop and service environments. Long-Term Battery Monitoring with Minimal Power Draw While battery testing captures condition at a specific point in time, leagend battery monitors are designed to show what happens between those tests. artigo.texto: BYD's Uber Fleet Deal Collides With a Home-Market Demand Puzzle Published on 09/25/2026 at 19:02 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD has handed investors two competing narratives in the space of a week: a landmark commercial fleet agreement with Uber that opens Western driveways without the cost of a retail sales push, and a deepening demand question mark in China that Citigroup flagged on September 16. The stock, at EUR 8.84, has shed 17 percent since the start of the year, and pre-market trading on Friday showed a further 2.3 percent decline to EUR 8.71 — uncomfortably close to its 52-week low of EUR 8.03. The Uber tie-up, announced Friday, is designed to cut operating costs for drivers and leaves the door open to future collaboration on autonomous vehicles. For a manufacturer navigating soft private demand in Western markets, commercial fleets offer scale without the heavy outlay of building a retail distribution network from scratch. Uber drivers gain access to BYD vehicles through standardized fleet programs, and the arrangement signals that Western mobility operators remain willing to lean on the group's manufacturing capacity despite geopolitical friction. The Operational Backbone Behind the Headline Whether that international push holds up depends less on delivery volumes than on something harder to build: a dependable, data-compliant service ecosystem. High overseas sales demand robust workshop networks, standardized after-sales processes and strict adherence to local data-security rules. Talks have centered on after-sales ecosystems, standardized repair data and cross-border data compliance, with Solera bringing connections to more than 200 manufacturers across over 120 countries. Get that infrastructure wrong and the costs mount quickly — delays, reputational damage and fleet customers such as mobility providers and leasing firms demanding short vehicle downtime and predictable repair bills. For investors, this operational foundation is becoming the real yardstick for whether overseas margins can hold. Manufacturing Milestones and a Charging Rollout Ahead of Schedule On the production side, BYD's Thai plant rolled its 100,000th new-energy vehicle off the line on September 21 — an Atto 3. The facility relies on a 95 percent Thai workforce and sources roughly 50 percent of components locally. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? Charging infrastructure is advancing in parallel. The company brought its 2,000th highway fast-charging station online at the Baoying service area in Jiangsu province, meeting its annual highway target early. As of that date, the network spanned 11,586 stations across 341 cities. Deutsche Bank analysts point to even bolder plans: 20,000 company-owned fast-charging points by the end of 2026 and a network of 90,000 stations by 2028. By year-end, BYD intends to complete 20,000 fast-charging stations in China overall. The commercial vehicle division added to the growth story on September 14, unveiling an expanded European lineup at the IAA Transportation show. That includes the heavy tractor unit ETT 44, capable of up to 600 kilometers of range on a 651 kilowatt-hour Blade battery. Should these products gain international traction, BYD wins valuable independence from the Chinese passenger-car market. Industrial momentum extends to energy storage. In Poland, project developer Greenvolt broke ground on the Siedlce large-scale storage project with a capacity of 2.4 gigawatt-hours, for which BYD Energy Storage is supplying the battery technology. Commercial operation is targeted for the end of 2027. In the premium segment, BYD's luxury brand Yangwang is preparing to launch a new upper-class sedan expected to carry the company's first solid-state batteries. Executive vice president Stella Li has said a first vehicle using the technology should hit the road in 2027, while the battery unit FinDreams plans limited production of sulfide solid-state cells that same year. Citigroup noted on September 16 that the share price decline has already outpaced earlier forecast revisions. The bank also made clear where the uncertainties lie: weaker-than-expected industry-wide retail sales in August and sluggish order intake in September are tempering expectations. If new business at home fails to fill high production capacity, margins come under inevitable pressure. The regulatory backdrop adds friction. On September 18, China's market regulator published a sweeping recall over potentially faulty brake-pedal bumpers. The action covers 58,026 units of the Tang line, 77,846 Tang DM vehicles, 7,023 Tang EVs and 40,316 Qin models. Components will be replaced free of charge, but the exercise ties up resources and puts quality questions in the spotlight. Trade policy poses a further headwind. Citigroup raised the prospect of cuts to China's export tax rebates and potential additional European Union tariffs on plug-in hybrids. If those hurdles take effect, BYD's profitable export business faces a marked slowdown. BYD at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now.
